apparatus.basis: Standard chapter heading; the Coptic word ⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ is preserved with only its initial ⲛ̄ⲕ lost in the gap, framed by decorative scribal flourishes (> · ... · <).

Editor restores [ⲙⲡ] before preserved ⲉϩⲱⲛⲉ̄. The compound ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲱⲛⲉ̄ (= Lyc ⲱⲛϩ̄ 'life,' confirmed by ⲡⲱⲛⲉ̄ 'life' in lines 8, 21 of this very page) yields 'his life,' with ⲙ̄ⲡ functioning as preposition 'in.'
Editor restores [ⲍ] within ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward' — directional preposition repeated immediately afterward in ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ 'inward to the church.'
Editor restores [ⲁⲩ] in ⲉⲧⲉϣⲁⲩⲉⲓ — Lycopolitan habitual relative ⲉⲧⲉ-ϣⲁⲩ-ⲉⲓ 'who habitually come.'
Editor restores [ⲉ] in ⲛⲉϩⲱⲏⲣⲉ 'his sons' (Lyc ⲛⲉϩ- possessive + ⲱⲏⲣⲉ = ϣⲏⲣⲉ 'son'); fits sequence 'sons / wife / kinsman.'
Editor restores [ⲟⲩ ⲉ] within ⲧⲟⲩ ⲉϣⲁϩⲕⲁ. The ⲧⲟⲩ completes ⲛ̄ϩⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧⲟⲩ 'his beloveds' from line 4; ⲉ begins relative-habitual ⲉϣⲁϩⲕⲁ 'who habitually places.'
Editor restores [ⲥ] completing ⲉⲓⲥ 'behold' — standard Coptic deictic particle opening the explicit application of the parable.
Editor restores [ⲥ] within ϣⲁⲩⲥⲁⲧϩⲟⲩ 'they habitually gather/select them' — Lyc habitual + verb of gathering with 3pl object.
Editor restores [ⲡ] within ⲉϩⲡⲱⲍ — qualitative ⲉ-(ⲩ)-ⲡⲱϩ 'which are ripe' (cf. ⲡⲱϩ 'ripen, mature' in agricultural register).
Editor restores [ⲗⲏ] completing ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ 'the church' — final two letters fall at line break, ⲥⲓⲁ visible at start of line 24.

Editor restores [ⲟ] completing ⲫⲛⲟ. The lexeme ⲫⲛⲟ recurs in line 23 (preserved as ⲡⲉϩⲫⲛⲟ 'his progress/journey') and here functions verbally — possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲛ 'transfer, proceed,' yielding 'his upward going proceeds inward unto him.' See note.

Editor restores [ϣⲁⲣⲡ] 'first, former.' Confirmed by line 30 antithetical pair 'ϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲙⲛ ⲍⲁⲉⲩⲉ' = 'first and last' — the contrast 'former sins' vs. 'latter sins' (ⲛ̄ⲍⲁⲉⲉⲩ in line 29) is the standard Manichaean confessional formula.
Editor restores [ⲟⲩⲛ ⲛ̄] — completion of ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward' + initial ⲛ̄ of ⲛ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ 'the first.' Eschatological ingathering formula.

notes.decision: Translated 'being gathered' — taking ⲥⲟ̄ϩⲣ as Lycopolitan qualitative of ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather, assemble' (cf. ⲡⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲥ 'the gatherer' in glossary; ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'the Gatherer-Inward'). The catechumen during his life is gathered into the holy church — ecclesiological language of incorporation.

Translated 'who has no equal value' — Coptic idiom 'has no value with-her' = 'is without comparable price, priceless.' The pearl's incomparable worth is the point of the parable: catechumens not returning to a body are of incomparable value, like the pearl described in Mani's Treasure of Life.

Translated 'gather' — most likely Lyc reflex of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'select, choose' or ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' with 3pl object suffix. Recurs in segment 23 paired with ⲃⲱⲗ 'release' as 'release them and gather them' — confirming the 'gather/collect' sense in the harvest typology.

Translated 'she chooses (the icon), and she goes for herself' — taking ⲛ̄ⲥ̄- as 3sg.f conjunctive both times: she (Mercy) chooses (one of the many icons in which she is likened) and goes inward for her own (sake/journey) to the country of the beautiful ones. Subject of all verbs is feminine ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ 'mercy.'

Translated 'his progress.' The lexeme ⲫⲛⲟ recurs both as noun here and as verb in segment 25 (where it governs 'inward unto him'). Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲛ 'transfer, pass over' nominalized; or related to ⲡⲱⲛⲉ 'go forth, proceed.' The agricultural-eschatological context (release, gathering, ascent) supports a 'progress, journey, transit' sense. Tentative.

Translated as verb 'proceeds' — same root as the noun in segment 24. The going-up of the catechumen 'proceeds inward unto him' = his ascension and purification together constitute the inward-leading movement. Preserves the directional-soteriological semantics central to the Manichaean ascent doctrine.

Translated 'a remission of sins.' ⲕⲁⲛⲁⲃⲉ = ⲕⲁ-ⲛⲁⲃⲉ (causative of ⲕⲱ 'leave, remit' + ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin') — the standard Coptic noun for 'remission/forgiveness of sins,' here as the object of the catechumen's prayer asked from God and Church.

Translated 'may be gathered inward.' ⲥⲱⲩⲍ = Lyc ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' (already in glossary as ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'Gatherer-Inward'). The future-relative construction expresses the soteriological aim of the confessional prayer: that all the catechumen's works — both former and latter sins, once forgiven — be gathered up and reckoned to his honor.
